Definition — Linear, sublinear and quadratic convergence
      
        Errors $e_k\to0$ converge linearly (geometrically) with rate $q\in(0,1)$ if $e_{k+1}\le q\,e_k$, so $e_k\le q^ke_0$; sublinearly if slower than every geometric rate, typically $e_k\le C/k^p$; quadratically if $e_{k+1}\le Ce_k^2$ (Newton's method near a solution).
original_row.statement_in_prose: Actual arbitrary error sequence satisfying each one-step inequality has every natural prefix bounded by q^n*error0, using genuine induction and nonnegative multiplication, not a chosen fixture.
hypotheses: q>=0; the stated one-step inequality holds at every natural index.
